industries.name: Financial & Insurance Services
industries.notes: London is one of the world's leading international financial centres. Financial services, alongside associated professional services, dominate the regional economy and are substantially larger relative to output than the UK average.

sources.publisher: House of Commons Library – Industries in the UK (ONS data)

industries.name: Professional, Scientific & Technical Services
industries.notes: Professional and technical sectors account for a disproportionately large share of London's output compared with the UK average, reflecting the concentration of legal, consulting, accounting, and management advisory firms.

sources.publisher: House of Commons Library – Industries in the UK (ONS data)

industries.name: Information Technology & Communications
industries.notes: London hosts a fast-growing tech sector centred on East London Tech City ('Silicon Roundabout') and hosts over 100 technology unicorns. IT and communications form a much larger share of London's output than the national average.

sources.publisher: House of Commons Library – Industries in the UK (ONS data)

industries.name: Real Estate & Construction
industries.notes: Real estate activities represent a significant component of London GVA. High property values and sustained development activity, including major projects such as Crossrail, underpin the sector's scale.

sources.publisher: Wikipedia – Economy of London

industries.name: Creative Industries, Media & Tourism
industries.notes: Media companies are heavily concentrated in London; the BBC, national newspapers, and film post-production (Soho) are key employers. Tourism generated £18.8bn in visitor expenditure in 2024, with nearly 36 million visits recorded.

landmarks.name: Tower Bridge
landmarks.visualNotes: Victorian Gothic bascule and suspension bridge spanning the River Thames, with its twin towers and pale stone facades instantly recognisable as London's most iconic riverside structure.

landmarks.name: Buckingham Palace
landmarks.visualNotes: Neoclassical royal residence at the end of The Mall, fronted by the Victoria Memorial and famous for the Changing of the Guard ceremony and its grand central balcony.

landmarks.name: The Shard
landmarks.visualNotes: Europe's tallest building at 310 metres, with a tapering glass façade of 11,000 panes that reflects the sky and city light, dominating the South Bank skyline above London Bridge.

landmarks.name: Canary Wharf
landmarks.visualNotes: London's secondary financial district on the Isle of Dogs, characterised by a dense cluster of glass skyscrapers including One Canada Square, surrounded by docklands waterways.

landmarks.name: Hyde Park
landmarks.visualNotes: 350-acre royal park in central London featuring the Serpentine lake, tree-lined avenues, Speaker's Corner, and open meadows providing a green counterpoint to the surrounding urban fabric.
